title: Workload-driven performance publish playbook with pin safeguards
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define and implement a playbook to publish Redwood-verified performance profiles that are validated against customer-like workload snippets. The playbook must produce a signed artifact, attach cost-normalized latency and throughput metrics, and include automatic pin safeguards (a temporary pin-lock window and deviation-alert rules) to prevent noisy republishing from regressing existing production behavior.
background: We publish performance profiles used by routing and autoscaling decisions. Current publish flow relies on synthetic benchmark suites that do not always match real customer request shapes. That leads to pinned profiles that later cause cost regressions or SLA misses when traffic distributions differ. We need a more workload-aware publish path and operational safety nets so teams can confidently publish and pin profiles without risking customer-facing regressions.
goals: 1) Add a workload-driven verification stage that runs sampled customer workload snippets (synthetic + representative traces) against candidate profiles. 2) Produce a signed publish artifact containing: latency P50/P95/P99, normalized cost per 1K tokens, throughput under target concurrency, and input-shape coverage notes. 3) Implement automatic pin-safeguards: ephemeral pin-lock window, deviation alerting, and simple rollback hints. 4) Update console publish UX and API to surface verification signals and signed artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: - Playbook executed end-to-end in staging: candidate model -> workload verification -> signed artifact generated -> profile visible in catalog with telemetry metrics. - Publish action supports optional "workload snippet" upload or reference to stored snippet. - Pin-safeguard: a pin-lock period (default 6 hours) prevents immediate forced republish; deviation alerts fire if sampled production telemetry deviates > 15% from published P95 latency or cost increases > 10% over baseline. - Signed artifact stored in registry with provenance link and hash. - Console shows verification status, snippet provenance, and an explicit 'force-republish' override requiring additional signoffs.
proposed_solution: 1) Extend onboarding runner to accept workload snippets (JSON lines of request shapes + payload sizes). Integrate with existing perf harness to compute cost-normalized metrics. 2) Generate a canonical publish artifact: flatfile JSON (signed with key rotation) containing metric values and snippet metadata. 3) In the publish pipeline, run a lightweight shadow run on a small reserved pool to validate throughput under representative concurrency. 4) Add a pin-safeguard controller: on publish, create a temporary pin-lock (configurable duration) and register deviation detectors that subscribe to trace sampling. 5) Expose UX: publish modal with snippet selector, verification summary, and a toggle to enable/disable pin-lock. 6) Document runbook for rollback and emergency unpin flows.
implementation_notes: - Leverage existing sample-run infrastructure used by perf-signature tests. - Use KMS-backed signing for artifacts (follow release key rotation policy). - Use normalized-cost formula used by billing team (tokens * hw-normalization factor) to compare across hardware. - Add new telemetry tags to production traces for profile provenance: profile_hash and published_at. - Keep default pin-lock conservative (6 hours) and allow enterprise customers to lengthen via publish policy.
risks: - Additional verification runs increase onboarding time and infra cost. Mitigation: run in parallel and cap sample size. - False positives in deviation alerts due to bursty traffic. Mitigation: use sliding-window aggregation and require sustained deviation for N minutes. - UX complexity causing publish friction. Mitigation: default sensible options and inline help.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement snippet ingestion and artifact signing; run end-to-end for 10 internal models. Phase 2 (beta): enable opt-in publish flow for performance team and two customer pilots. Phase 3 (gradual): default the workload-driven verification for all publishes with telemetry-based opt-out for legacy workflows. Monitor "publish fail rate" and time-to-publish during ramp.
